extracted.intended_audience: LaTeX users and authors preparing documents with substantial mathematics who will use the amsmath package
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for using the amsmath LaTeX package to produce well-structured, correctly spaced, and properly numbered mathematical formulas and displays. Covers package options, displayed-equation environments, math constructs (matrices, fractions, accents, delimiters, arrows, etc.), error diagnostics, and conversion/help procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and recommended use of amsmath
rubrics_metrics.description: The amsmath package provides miscellaneous enhancements for improving the information structure and printed output of documents that contain mathematical formulas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use amsmath to get better displayed-equation structures, operator-name definition, multiline subscripts, subordinate equation numbers, correct spacing around relation symbols, and other refinements versus basic LaTeX.

rubrics_metrics.name: Package composition and related packages
rubrics_metrics.description: amsmath is distributed with small auxiliary packages (amstext, amsopn, amsbsy, amscd, amsxtra). amsmath incorporates amstext, amsopn, and amsbsy; amscd and amsxtra are available separately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Load the specific auxiliary packages only when you need their features (e.g., amscd for simple commutative diagrams). Prefer bm over amsbsy for bold math symbols.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer align / equation+split over eqnarray
rubrics_metrics.description: Although eqnarray remains available, it is better to use align or equation+split instead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: amsmath fixes spacing and numbering problems found in eqnarray; using align or split yields correct spacing around relation symbols and avoids overprinting of numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Displayed-equation environments and starred forms
rubrics_metrics.description: amsmath supplies environments: equation, gather, multline, split, align, flalign, alignat (and starred versions). Except split, each has starred (unnumbered) and unstarred (numbered) forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suppress numbering on a particular line with \notag or override with \tag{...} or \tag* (literal text).

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment ampersand placement convention
rubrics_metrics.description: In alignment structures (split, align and variants), relation symbols have an & before them but not after—unlike eqnarray.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Putting the & after the relation symbol will interfere with normal spacing; put & before the relation symbol.

rubrics_metrics.name: split environment usage
rubrics_metrics.description: The split environment is a special subordinate form used only inside another displayed structure; it provides alignment among split lines but provides no numbering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use split only as the entire body of an enclosing structure (equation, align, or gather). It cannot be used inside multline and supplies no equation number itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: multline environment semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: multline is used for single equations that don't fit on one line: first line left, last line right, middle lines centered (unless fleqn). Single equation number only (placed on last line or first line depending on reqno/leqno).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use \shoveleft and \shoveright to force a middle line to left or right; change \multlinegap with \setlength or \addtolength.

rubrics_metrics.name: gather environment semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: gather is for a group of consecutive equations with no mutual alignment; each is centered separately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equations inside gather are separated by \\; any equation inside gather may itself consist of a split environment.

rubrics_metrics.name: align and alignat environments for mutual alignment
rubrics_metrics.description: align is for two or more equations when vertical alignment is desired (e.g., aligning = signs). alignat allows explicit specification of horizontal space between equation columns and takes argument equal to number of equation columns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use extra ampersands to create multiple equation columns; count columns as (max &s + 1)/2 to choose argument for alignat.

rubrics_metrics.name: Variants gathered/aligned/alignedat for use as building blocks
rubrics_metrics.description: The -ed variants (gathered, aligned, alignedat) produce a structure whose total width is the contents' natural width (not full line width), making them usable inside other expressions (like cases).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These variants accept optional [t] or [b] for vertical positioning, and are useful when parentheses or other enclosing material are needed around aligned groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cases constructions and use of \text inside math
rubrics_metrics.description: A cases environment exists for piecewise definitions; use \text for words within math to produce correct text formatting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nested math formulas are allowed inside cases; prefer \text over \mbox for readability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tag placement and \raisetag
rubrics_metrics.description: amsmath tries to avoid overprinting equation numbers and may move tags up or down; use \raisetag{<dimen>} to fine-tune the vertical position of the current equation number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat \raisetag adjustments as fine tuning to be done near final document layout; example: \raisetag{6pt} moves the tag up by 6 points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertical spacing and page-break control in multiline displays
rubrics_metrics.description: Use \\[<dimen>] to add vertical space between lines. Page breaks between equation lines are normally disallowed; use \displaybreak (optional [0..4]) before \\ to allow/force breaks. \allowdisplaybreaks[1..4] in preamble allows page breaks with increasing permissiveness; \allowdisplaybreaks[0] or omission disallows them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: \displaybreak[0] permits but discourages a break; \displaybreak (no arg) equals [4] and forces. \allowdisplaybreaks[1] allows breaks but avoids them when possible. Note: split, aligned, gathered, and alignedat wrap contents in an unbreakable box and are not affected by \displaybreak/\allowdisplaybreaks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interrupting a display with \intertext
rubrics_metrics.description: Use \intertext to insert one or two short lines of text inside a multi-line display while preserving alignment; \intertext may only appear immediately after \\ or \\*.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not end the display and restart; \intertext preserves alignment across the interruption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equation numbering placement options (leqno, reqno, fleqn)
rubrics_metrics.description: Package/class options: leqno places equation numbers on the left; reqno on the right; fleqn positions equations at a fixed indent from the left margin rather than centered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are selected as package options (or via documentclass options) and affect default placement and layout.

rubrics_metrics.name: Package options controlling limits placement (centertags, tbtags, sumlimits, nosumlimits, intlimits, nointlimits, namelimits, nonamelimits)
rubrics_metrics.description: centertags (default) vertically center equation numbers on split equations; tbtags aligns numbers with last/first line. sumlimits/nosumlimits control placement of subscripts/superscripts on sum-type symbols; intlimits/nointlimits similarly for integrals; namelimits/nonamelimits affect operator names like det, lim with traditional display limits behavior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify options in \usepackage (e.g., \usepackage[intlimits]{amsmath}). Some of these are normally set via \documentclass and need not be repeated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numbering hierarchy and \numberwithin
rubrics_metrics.description: Use \numberwithin{equation}{section} (or any counter) to tie equation numbering to section numbering and automatically reset the equation counter at each new section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is simpler than manual \renewcommand{\theequation} and \setcounter manipulations; \numberwithin works with any counter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-references to equations via \eqref
rubrics_metrics.description: \eqref{<label>} produces the equation number with parentheses automatically, e.g., (3.2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer \eqref over \ref when referencing equations to ensure consistent parentheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subordinate numbering via subequations environment
rubrics_metrics.description: The subequations environment makes it easy to number a group of equations as (4.9a), (4.9b), ...; a \label immediately after \begin{subequations} references the parent number 4.9 (not 4.9a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use counters parentequation and equation as usual; change subordinate numbering style using standard LaTeX counter style commands if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defining new operator names (\DeclareMathOperator and \operatorname)
rubrics_metrics.description: Define new function/operator names that behave like \sin or \lim using \DeclareMathOperator{\xxx}{xxx}; use the * form (\DeclareMathOperator*) to place subscripts/superscripts in limits position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The name text is printed in a pseudo-text mode; hyphens and asterisks behave like text characters. Use \operatorname{...} inline when you don't want a new command definition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modular arithmetic macros (\mod, \bmod, \pmod, \pod)
rubrics_metrics.description: amsmath provides \mod (omits parentheses), \bmod, \pmod (adjusting spacing for display vs inline), and \pod (omits 'mod' and keeps parentheses) to handle special spacing of 'mod' notation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the variant that matches the traditional notation and spacing you require; \pmod spacing adapts in non-display mode.

rubrics_metrics.name: Text in math: use of \text
rubrics_metrics.description: The \text command typesets text fragments inside math mode similar to \mbox but more convenient (no need to change size commands for subscripts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ..._{\text{word or phrase}} for readable text in subscripts or display formulas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matrix environments and MaxMatrixCols
rubrics_metrics.description: pmatrix, bmatrix, Bmatrix, vmatrix, Vmatrix and matrix provide matrix constructions with built-in delimiters and more economical spacing than array. Default maximum centered columns is determined by counter MaxMatrixCols (normal value = 10).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you need left/right alignment or special column formats, use array. Adjust MaxMatrixCols with \setcounter if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: smallmatrix for inline small matrices
rubrics_metrics.description: Use smallmatrix to typeset a small matrix suitable for use within text; delimiters must be provided externally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: smallmatrix has no pmatrix/bmatrix variants; use \bigl( \begin{smallmatrix} ... \end{smallmatrix} \bigr) for inline parentheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ellipsis (dots) semantic commands
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer semantically oriented commands: \dotsc (dots with commas), \dotsb (dots with binary operators/relations), \dotsm (multiplication dots), \dotsi (dots with integrals), \dotso (other dots).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using these commands makes it possible to adapt to different publisher conventions automatically. The defaults follow AMS conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Math spacing commands and \mspace
rubrics_metrics.description: amsmath extends math spacing commands (\,, \:, \;, \quad, \qquad, \!, etc.) and provides \mspace to use math units (1mu = 1/18em) for fine control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both spelled-out and abbreviated forms are robust and usable outside math; use \mspace{-18.0mu} to emulate a negative \quad, for example.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use \nobreakdash to prevent linebreak after hyphen/dash
rubrics_metrics.description: The command \nobreakdash suppresses the possibility of a linebreak after the following hyphen or dash (useful for 'pages 1--9' or 'p-adic').
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
For frequent use define macros like 
ewcommand{\p}{$p$
obreakdash} or 
ewcommand{\Ndash}{
obreakdash--} to simplify notation; zero-width space can be used to allow hyphenation in subsequent word.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improved accents: \dddot and \ddddot, and third-party accents
rubrics_metrics.description: amsmath provides \dddot and \ddddot for triple and quadruple dot accents and improves second-accent placement; amsxtra provides \sphat and \sptilde for superscripted hat/tilde.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For arbitrary symbol accenting or under-accents see the accents package by Javier Bezos.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjusting root index position with \leftroot and \uproot
rubrics_metrics.description: \leftroot and \uproot allow fine adjustment of the position of the root index in \sqrt[...]{...}, e.g., \sqrt[\leftroot{-2}\uproot{2}\beta]{k}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use small integer arguments to move the index slightly left/right and up/down for better visual placement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boxed formulas with \boxed
rubrics_metrics.description: Use \boxed{<math>} to put a box around a math expression (like \fbox but in math mode).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for emphasizing displayed formulas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Over/under arrows and extensible arrows
rubrics_metrics.description: amsmath provides additional arrow commands: \overleftarrow, \overrightarrow, \overleftrightarrow, \underleftarrow, \underrightarrow, \underleftrightarrow and extensible arrows \xleftarrow and \xrightarrow that take optional subscript and mandatory superscript arguments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use \xleftarrow{...} and \xrightarrow[under]{over} to create arrows sized to their scripts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affixing symbols: \overset and \underset
rubrics_metrics.description: \overset{<symbol>}{<base>} places a symbol above another; \underset does the analog for placing beneath.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: More general than \stackrel; can be used with relations or other symbols.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fractions, binomials and \genfrac
rubrics_metrics.description: amsmath provides \frac, and shorthand \dfrac and \tfrac for display/textstyle fractions; \binom, \dbinom, \tbinom; and a generalized fraction command \genfrac{left}{right}{thickness}{mathstyle}{num}{den}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you repeatedly use a particular \genfrac configuration, define a meaningful macro for readability and publisher compatibility. Primitive primitives like \over issue warnings under amsmath.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continued fractions via \cfrac
rubrics_metrics.description: Use \cfrac{num}{den} (and optional [l] or [r]) to typeset continued fractions with better results than nested \frac.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use \cfrac[l] or \cfrac[r] to left/right place numerators for spacing control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Smash options \smash[t] and \smash[b]
rubrics_metrics.description: amsmath extends \smash with optional arguments t and b to 'smash' only the top or only the bottom of a subformula while retaining the other dimension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful to equalize adjacent radical symbol sizes or to fine-tune vertical extents without killing both height and depth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delimiter sizing and 'big' delimiter commands
rubrics_metrics.description: Automatic sizing with \left and \right can be coarse; use \bigl, \bigr, \Bigl, \Bigr, \biggl, \biggr, \Biggl, \Biggr to pick delimiter sizes more precisely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'big' sizes for (a) cumulative operators with limits, (b) nested delimiters to aid visual nesting, and (c) slightly oversize objects in running text to avoid excessive line spread. amsmath scales these properly across LaTeX font sizes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertical bar notations: \lvert, \rvert, \lVert, \rVert and consistent macros
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide \lvert, \rvert, \lVert, \rVert to avoid overloading the plain '|' character; recommend defining document macros \abs and \norm mapping to these commands for consistent usage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose one meaning for '|' across the document (e.g., absolute value) and use paired delimiter macros for 'left'/'right' behavior: \providecommand{\abs}[1]{\lvert#1\rvert}.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiline subscripts/superscripts: \substack and subarray
rubrics_metrics.description: Use \substack{...} to create multiline subscripts/superscripts in sums/products; subarray environment allows alignment specification (e.g., left-aligned lines).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these when limits require stacked conditions, e.g., \sum_{\substack{0\le i\le m\\0<j<n}}.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corner superscripts/subscripts on large operators: \sideset
rubrics_metrics.description: \sideset places symbols at the corner positions of large operator symbols (e.g., adding a prime to a sum symbol); intended for sum-class operators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not designed for arbitrary operators; use primarily to place primes or other corner symbols on \sum and similar.

rubrics_metrics.name: Math-font commands and recommended usage
rubrics_metrics.description: amsmath documents discuss recommended use of math font commands (\mathbb, \mathbf, \mathcal, \mathfrak, etc.) and tools for bold math (recommend bm package).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer semantic naming and consistent font choices; use \DeclareMathOperator for text-like operator names rather than \newcommand{\Hom}{\mbox{Hom}}.

rubrics_metrics.name: Error messages: diagnosis and suggested fixes (font TFMs)
rubrics_metrics.description: If you see errors like 'Font OMX/cmex/m/n/7=cmex7 not loadable' or 'Math formula deleted: Insufficient extension fonts', it indicates missing font sizes/TFM files. amsmath offers a temporary workaround cmex10 option.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: First try to obtain missing fonts from your TeX distribution or CTAN. As a temporary workaround add \usepackage[cmex10]{amsmath} to force 10pt cmex; better to install correct fonts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Error message: Missing number, treated as zero
rubrics_metrics.description: Often caused by forgetting number argument to alignat environment or other numeric-required arguments; e.g., \begin{alignat} instead of \begin{alignat}{2}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check for missing numeric arguments (alignat, etc.) or stray '[' after \\ which TeX interprets as vertical space specification; bracing the argument (e.g., {[f,g]}) can avoid misinterpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Error message: Missing \right. inserted
rubrics_metrics.description: Occurs when trying to insert a linebreak inside a \left-\right pair in multline/split; TeX inserts \right. to try to recover.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Solutions: (1) use explicit 'big' delimiters instead of \left/\right; or (2) break the \left-\right pair with null delimiters (e.g., \left(...\right. \\ \left. ... \right)) combined with \vphantom or \smash to match sizes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Error message: Paragraph ended before \xxx was complete / Runaway argument
rubrics_metrics.description: Typically caused by a missing '}' or a misspelled environment name (e.g., \end{multiline} instead of \end{multline}), or by defining abbreviations for environment names that are not safe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check matching braces and correct environment names. Avoid using short abbreviations like \bal / \eal for complex displayed environments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Error: Unknown package option
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicates a misspelled option name or an option that does not exist in the package (example: 'intlim' typo).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check documentation for correct option names and spelling before use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Error: Old Plain-TeX forms (\pmatrix etc.) are deprecated
rubrics_metrics.description: Old forms like \pmatrix{...} are Plain-TeX syntax and are not to be used with amsmath; use \begin{pmatrix} ... \end{pmatrix}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replace plain-TeX shorthand with LaTeX environment form to conform to amsmath expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Error: Erroneous nesting of equation structures
rubrics_metrics.description: Some amsmath structures (align, alignat, etc.) are designed for top-level use and generally cannot be nested inside other displayed structures; exception: align may be used inside gather.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid nesting top-level alignment environments. Use the -ed variants (aligned, gathered) if you need inner aligned blocks inside other displays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Warnings: foreign commands like \over
rubrics_metrics.description: Primitive TeX generalized fraction commands (\over, \atop, \above) are deprecated under amsmath; amsmath issues a warning suggesting \frac or \genfrac.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replace uses of \over, \atop, \above with \frac, \genfrac, \binom, etc., to get LaTeX-native behavior and avoid warnings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Warning: Cannot use 'split' here
rubrics_metrics.description: The split environment must be the entire body of certain enclosing structures; it is not allowed where printed material occurs before or after it in the same enclosing structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure split is used as the entire content of an enclosing equation or align line; otherwise use aligned or other appropriate constructs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common wrong-output pitfall: reversed \numberwithin arguments
rubrics_metrics.description:
If section numbers appear as 0.1, 5.1, 8.1 instead of 1, 2, 3, you may have reversed arguments to 
umberwithin (e.g., 
umberwithin{section}{equation} instead of 
umberwithin{equation}{section}).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Swap the arguments to the intended form to correct numbering hierarchy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Converting existing documents (plain LaTeX -> amsmath)
rubrics_metrics.description: Adding \usepackage{amsmath} usually preserves most document behavior but amsmath suppresses page breaks inside multi-line displays; you may need to add \allowdisplaybreaks[1] in preamble to restore breaks in eqnarray or convert eqnarray to align/multline/split.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider replacing eqnarray with align or split and use \DeclareMathOperator instead of \newcommand{\Hom}{\mbox{Hom}} for semantic clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Getting help: information to include when reporting problems
rubrics_metrics.description: When reporting amsmath problems include (1) the source file reduced to minimal size reproducing the problem; (2) a LaTeX log file showing the error message and version numbers of document class and option files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Send problem reports to AMS Technical Support or the addresses listed; providing minimal examples and logs speeds diagnosis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bibliographic and further reading recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: References to AMSFonts, AMS-LaTeX instructions, amsthm documentation, The LaTeX Companion, The TeXbook, and other resources are provided for deeper understanding and related tools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult referenced documents for font issues, AMS document classes, theorem handling, and advanced TeX/LaTeX topics.
